precepts.text: Was Christ ever confused about his position and role with the Father? I can of mine own self do nothing: I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me. Christ understands his role and position, and Christ tells us the husband is the head of the wife. So why is there still so much confusion? Somebody does not believe like they say they do.
precepts.point: If you are scared of your wife, you cannot get out here and cast down the lies of the nations and bring us out of this captivity when you are scared to deal with your own house.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Is anybody confused on the order? Then why are there so many problems in Israel, so much confusion about the husband's position and the wife's position? Because pride has made its way in, and confusion has set itself in the house.

“and the head of Christ is God”. Was Christ ever confused, at any moment in his life, about his position and role with the Father? He said: “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

Christ said, I am doing exactly as the Father told me to do. Is he doing what he wants? No. Christ understands his role and his position. And Christ now tells us the husband is the head of the wife. So why is there still so much confusion? Somebody does not believe like they say they do.

It happens on both sides of the room. Brother, because of your lack of leadership, because you are non-confrontational and passive and don't want no smoke, she raises her voice and you cower; she walks by shoulder-bumping you, and you can't raise your voice in your own house. All because you gave up your position. Some brothers want to be mama's boys: you didn't want a wife, you wanted a mom. If Christ submits to the head over him, the husband must take his place under Christ, and the wife her place under her husband.

precepts.text: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
“I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.” Whatever Job did not know, he searched out. Sometimes brothers try to fake stuff. Don’t fake it. Job said, if I did not know it, I searched it out.

Christ said it: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.”

We have to get to that point. Search it out. Get the Who’s Who with the Apocrypha, get your Zondervan Bible dictionary, get the complete works of Josephus, get your concordance, and do your own work. Before you ask us a question, how about you search it out, and then ask your question after you have done research on it. That is what Job did with every cause he did not know.

precepts.text: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. When Paul presented the truth of Christ, they searched the scriptures daily to see if what Paul taught was accurate. That is what we have to do.
precepts.point: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me. Our job is to search the scriptures. The nations do not search the scriptures; they leave their searching from Matthew to Revelation with their misunderstanding through Christianity. If you start from Genesis, you find out that salvation and rulership of the earth is for the Israelites through Christ.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“Search the scriptures.” Our job is to search the scriptures. The nations don't; they leave their scripture searching to Matthew through Revelation with their misunderstanding from Christianity. If you start from Genesis, you find out that salvation and rulership of the earth is only for the Israelites through Christ. The Bereans show how it is done: “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

When Paul presented the truth of Christ to them, they did not just take it; they searched the scriptures daily to see whether what Paul was teaching was accurate according to the scriptures. That is what made them more noble, and that is what we have to do.

The scriptures they searched were the same ones Christ said “testify of me.” Searching them daily with a ready mind is how the truth of Christ is proved.

precepts.text: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter. When God conceals something in parables, metaphors, and allegories, it is our job to figure out what the Lord means.
precepts.point: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me. Our job is to search the scriptures. The nations do not search the scriptures; they leave their searching from Matthew to Revelation with their misunderstanding through Christianity. If you start from Genesis, you find out that salvation and rulership of the earth is for the Israelites through Christ.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.” When God conceals something, it is in parable form, metaphors and allegories, and it is our job to figure out what the Lord means by A, B and C.

That is why we must search. Read Jeremiah 48, “against Moab”, or Jeremiah 49, “Concerning the Ammonites”, and unless you search the scriptures and pray to the Lord, you'll say, I don't know who Moab is, I don't know who the Ammonites are, I don't know who Gad is, I'm confused, so I'll stick to Matthew through Revelation. That's what the churches do. Christians don't know and Muslims don't know, confused and discombobulated, unable to identify these nations today.

The honour of kings is to search it out: to find who Moab, Ammon, Gad and Asia are today. The matter is concealed, but it is there for those who search.

What God has kept secret and then revealed is for our children and our children's children. What we bring out in the scriptures is meant for our sons and daughters; teach them, and do not let this truth fall by the wayside.

precepts.why:
“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

What God has kept secret and then revealed to us is for our children and our children's children forever. So what we bring out in the scriptures is meant for our sons and our daughters. Teach them. Don't let this truth fall by the wayside, with your sons and daughters worshipping Caesar Borgia all over again. That would be a detriment to you and your family.

Searching the scriptures is not only for ourselves. What the Lord reveals by it belongs to us and to our children, so that we and they may do all the words of this law.

precepts.text: I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me. Christ does not do what he wants to; he does what the Father tells him to. Yet the scripture says he and his Father are one.
precepts.point: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord. We start with the order first. We as a body have to be one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this congregation: because we are one.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
How are Christ and the Father one? Christ does what his Father tells him to do. “I can of mine own self do nothing”: Christ said it himself. “as I hear, I judge”: as I'm told, that's what I do. “and my judgment is just”: the things he does are justified, “because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He didn't do what he wanted to do; he did what the Father told him to do. You see how that works? He says, I don't do what I want to, I do what the Father tells me to, and yet the scripture says he and his Father are one.

That is the oneness of Deuteronomy 6:4. Being one is not everybody doing their own will; it is every member doing the will of the one who is over him. That is how Christ is one with the Father, and how the body is one with Christ.

precepts.text: I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto him that sent me.” Who sent Jesus? Christ answers it himself: “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He did not come on his own errand. He was sent from his Father, and he sought only the Father's will. And that will was to gather the twelve tribes of Israel: other sheep he must bring in, that there might be one fold and one shepherd. The gathering began when Christ came and began to teach, and his death was the beginning of the twelve tribes being brought back together.

So when he says he goes “unto him that sent me”, he is going back to the Father whose will he came to do. What that will was, the prophets had already written, and Isaiah 11 shows it.

precepts.text: Had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. When Moses wrote in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy about the Lord, that person Moses was talking about was always Christ.
precepts.point: For my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them: these words are the Lord's spirit.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Christ says, “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” Moses wrote of Christ. When you read it in Genesis, in Exodus, in Numbers, in Deuteronomy, right through the scriptures, the one Moses was talking about when he wrote “the Lord said” and “the Lord did” was always Christ. That is why Christ can say that if you believed Moses you would have believed him.

“But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” The writings of Moses and the words of Christ stand together; to reject one is to reject the other.

This is the book Isaiah sends us to: “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” Read with Hebrews 10:7, where Christ says “in the volume of the book it is written of me”, it shows that the whole book of the Lord, from the writings of Moses on, is written of Christ. So when we seek out of that book and read, we are reading of him, and “no one of these shall fail”: everything written there is going to come to pass.

precepts.text: Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. You never heard the Father's voice at any time in history. So that voice our people heard in the wilderness, and that shape the elders saw: that was Christ.
precepts.point: Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice: whose voice did they hear from the heavens? That was Christ's voice, speaking the commandments. And upon earth he shewed thee his great fire: when the Lord came down in Exodus, only the seventy elders saw his majesty; everybody else saw fire.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee”. Whose voice did they hear from the heavens? Some people think that is the Father. No, that was Christ's voice. That was the Lord speaking, the one who came down and gave us the commandments.

Christ said it himself: “And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.” The Father sent Christ and bore witness of him, but at no time in history have you ever heard the Father's voice, and you never saw his shape.

So the voice our people heard in the wilderness, out of the midst of the fire, was Christ's. And the shape the seventy elders saw when the Lord came down was Christ. It was always the Lord, always Christ there: the rock and the chariot that followed us, the one who came down and smote the Egyptians, the same one who will come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt that we are living in today.

precepts.text: The Jews sought to kill Jesus for making himself equal with God; he was a god on earth yet said the Father is greater than I.
precepts.point: Christ had to be made lower than the angels so that he could die. In his angelic form he would be immortal; he had to come after the seed of Abraham, David, and Joseph, from sperm, so that he could taste death for every Israelite man.

note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
Christ said the Father is greater than he, yet he was a god on earth. After he healed the man at the pool, “Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” The man told the Jews it was Jesus, “And therefore did the Jews persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day.”

“But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work. Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.”

The Jews sought to kill Jesus for making himself equal with God. He was a god on earth, the son of man crowned with glory and honour with all things under his feet, and still he said the Father is greater than I. Both are true: he is the Son with dominion, and the Father is above him.

precepts.text: Are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day? Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
precepts.point: He had broken no sabbath. He answers them elsewhere out of their own practice: they circumcise on the sabbath so that the law of Moses be not broken, and a man made every whit whole is greater than that.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
The Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to slay him, “because he had done these things on the sabbath day.” He had broken no sabbath. He answers them elsewhere out of their own practice: “Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.”

“If a man on the sabbath day receive circumcision, that the law of Moses should not be broken; are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day?” They circumcise on the sabbath so that the law of Moses be not broken, and a man made every whit whole is greater than that.

“Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.” By the appearance, he worked on the sabbath; by righteous judgment, he made a man whole, and that broke no sabbath.

precepts.text: We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness, and maketh his boast that God is his father.
precepts.point: That attitude toward a just man was written down long before.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“My Father worketh hitherto, and I work.” They sought the more to kill him, because he “said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.” That attitude toward a just man was written down long before.

Solomon gives the words of the wicked against the just: “We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and maketh his boast that God is his father.”

He maketh his boast that God is his father. That is the very thing the Jews held against Christ: he said God was his Father. And he abstained from their ways as from filthiness, and esteemed them as counterfeits. Their hatred of him was foretold word for word.

precepts.text: Being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit.
precepts.point: As the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will. To quicken is to make alive, and it covers both the raising of the dead and the making alive of men dead in their sins.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will.” To quicken is to make alive. Peter uses the word of Christ himself: “For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”.

Put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: made alive. The Father raised up the Son; and the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do, and so the Son quickeneth whom he will. Quickening covers both the raising of the dead and the making alive of men dead in their sins.

precepts.text: We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.
precepts.point: He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. That is why men stand before the judgment seat of Christ: “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.”

All judgment is committed unto the Son, so the judgment seat is Christ's, and every one receives there the things done in his body, good or bad. That is also why “all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.”

precepts.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
precepts.point: He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.” Paul says who those are: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

No condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus; and they are marked by how they walk, not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. He that hears his word and believes on him that sent him is passed from death unto life, and does not come into condemnation.

precepts.text: Many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
precepts.point: All that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.” Daniel saw the same two resurrections: “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Some to everlasting life, some to shame and everlasting contempt: the resurrection of life and the resurrection of damnation. “The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.” That happened before their eyes with Lazarus, and it reaches forward to the last judgment, when all that are in the graves hear his voice and awake, as Daniel wrote.

precepts.text: Beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
precepts.point: They could not match the prophecies to the life being lived in front of them. He had to open the scriptures himself, from Moses through all the prophets, to shew what they said of him.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.” The scriptures testify of Christ, but they could not match the prophecies to the life being lived in front of them.

He had to open the scriptures himself: “And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.” From Moses through all the prophets, he shewed what they said of him. The scriptures they searched were the ones testifying of him all along, and “ye will not come to me, that ye might have life.”

precepts.text: A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear. Every soul which will not hear that prophet shall be destroyed from among the people.
precepts.point: If ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words? A man who will not take what Moses wrote will not take Christ either.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” Peter shows what Moses wrote: “For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you.”

Moses wrote of a prophet raised up of their brethren, like unto him, and that prophet is Christ: him shall ye hear. Then the warning: “And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people.” That is why Christ says, “there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.” Moses himself wrote that every soul which will not hear that prophet shall be destroyed. Refusing Christ is refusing Moses.

precepts.text: If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
precepts.point: If ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words? A man who will not take what Moses wrote will not take Christ either.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” A man who will not take what Moses wrote will not take Christ either. Christ says it again in the parable: “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.”

It is the same order. Moses and the prophets come first; a man who will not hear them will not be persuaded even by one risen from the dead. They trusted in Moses, yet believed not his writings, and so they did not believe the words of the one Moses wrote of.

points: A man had been there thirty and eight years and had no man to put him in. Wilt thou be made whole?

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: Rise, take up thy bed, and walk. He did not have to wait for the water at all, and immediately he was made whole. And on the same day was the sabbath.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: The first thing said to a man healed after thirty-eight years is that it is not lawful for him to carry his bed. Not one word about the healing.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee. The healing came with a charge, and that charge is the keeping of the commandments.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: He had broken no sabbath. He answers them elsewhere out of their own practice: they circumcise on the sabbath so that the law of Moses be not broken, and a man made every whit whole is greater than that.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: The Jews persecuted him, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: My Father worketh hitherto, and I work. They sought the more to kill him, because he said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: As the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will. To quicken is to make alive, and it covers both the raising of the dead and the making alive of men dead in their sins.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: The Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son, which is why men stand before the judgment seat of Christ.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. That happened before their eyes with Lazarus, and it reaches forward to the last judgment.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: All that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: Ye sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the truth. He was a burning and a shining light, and ye were willing for a season to rejoice in his light.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: But I have greater witness than that of John: the works which the Father hath given me to finish bear witness of me.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.
They could not match the prophecies to the life being lived in front of them. He had to open the scriptures himself, from Moses through all the prophets, to shew what they said of him.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust. For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: If ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words? A man who will not take what Moses wrote will not take Christ either.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son
